annotator.notes: Student initially confuses total time with reading time; tutor guides them through step-by-step conversion and calculation.

task_context.problem_statement: Rob planned on spending three hours reading in preparation for his literature exam. If he ends up spending only three-quarters of this time reading, and he reads a page every fifteen minutes, how many pages did he read in this time?
task_context.reference_solution:
1 hour is 60 minutes so 3 hours is 3*60 = <<3*60=180>>180 minutes
Three-quarters of 180 minutes is (3/4)*180 = <<(3/4)*180=135>>135 minutes
He spends 15 minutes on 1 page so he will spend 135 minutes on 135/15 = <<135/15=9>>9 pages
#### 9

messages.content: I'm stuck on this problem: Rob planned on spending three hours reading in preparation for his literature exam. If he ends up spending only three-quarters of this time reading, and he reads a page every fifteen minutes, how many pages did he read in this time? I think the answer is 12. Is that right?
I can help you check that! To make sure we're on the right track, could you walk me through how you arrived at 12 pages? I'd like to see your steps.
Well, he planned for 3 hours, and 3 hours is 180 minutes. Then I just divided 180 by 15 minutes per page, which gave me 12. So he read 12 pages.

I see what you did there. You calculated how many pages he would have read if he spent the full 3 hours reading. However, take another look at the problem: did he actually spend the full three hours reading?
Oh, I missed that part. It says he only spent three-quarters of that time. So I need to find three-quarters of 180 minutes first, right?
That's exactly right. What is three-quarters of 180 minutes?
Okay, 180 divided by 4 is 45, and 45 times 3 is 135. So he spent 135 minutes reading.
Perfect. Now that you have the actual time he spent reading, how does that change the number of pages he finished?
I divide the 135 minutes by the 15 minutes it takes per page. 135 / 15 = 9. So the answer is 9 pages!
Spot on! You correctly adjusted for the time spent and then calculated the pages based on his reading speed. Great job working through that.
